fit: Complete issue and independent clinical vignettes
assessment: Pages 209 and 251 describe an insulinoma evaluation with visual history and a suspected grapefruit–medication interaction with acute visual and auditory hallucinations. They are separate members and neither compares dried-fig intake in Parkinson disease.

fit: Prospectively assessed dementia with imaging and autopsy
assessment: The 20 autopsy cases include eight Lewy body dementia cases. Visual hallucinations were once only in 2/8 vs 1/12 and persistent in 4/8 vs 5/12. The authors report no significant group difference. The study does not compare food exposure or count repeated episodes.

fit: Conference records with separate clinical endpoints
assessment: Poster P64 uses visual symptoms as background to a head-drop case. Poster P102 reports psychiatric outcomes after subthalamic stimulation in eight Parkinson cases without a separately coded visual episode rate. No member provided a dried-fig comparison.

fit: Author abstract of diagnostic tracer and perfusion comparison
assessment: The 7 versus 6 clinical dementia groups showed different imaging patterns. The abstract mentions hallucinations in background and does not measure episodes after food exposure.

fit: Author abstract of autopsy-linked clinical imaging case
assessment: A single dementia case showed low presynaptic tracer uptake and was confirmed as Lewy body dementia at autopsy. Whether that case appears in the later series remains unverified. The abstract records no separately assessed visual symptoms or dried-fig intake.

fit: Clinical dementia and Parkinson group imaging comparison
assessment: The 164-person cohort measures scan readings against clinical diagnosis. The imaging differentiation between Lewy body and Alzheimer dementia does not measure visual episodes or a response to food.

fit: Statistical imaging analysis across clinical groups
assessment: FP-CIT image maps show binding reductions in Parkinson and Lewy body dementia groups. The endpoint is imaging, and overlap with the other 2004 imaging paper remains unverified.
